answer: Like an ocean deepening under tidal pressure, our consensus weaves each peer through a cryptographic web of trust. A rogue identity arrives like a hollow zephyr, unable to anchor. When minting identities, each agent must bind a stake-weighted thread of verified reciprocal interactions. Forging false majorities demands superlinear attacker cost via quadratic slashing and trust-graph decay, dissolving Sybil swarms into oblivion.
